evidence.claim: Article 80 vests the executive power of the federation in a single individual called the President of the United Mexican States.
evidence.title: Constitución Política de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos
evidence.excerpt: Article 80 vests the executive power of the federation in a single individual called the President of the United Mexican States.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official constitutional text; stable and authoritative for office structure.
evidence.period_fit: Directly applicable to 2022 as the governing constitutional framework.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Structural authority held by AMLO as president; this does not itself show any nuclear-specific personal choice.
contrary_evidence: Mexico is non-nuclear, so this office does not imply command over a nuclear arsenal.
Formal executive authority does not prove operational control over civilian nuclear safety details.

evidence.claim: Article 89, fraction X, gives the president authority to direct foreign policy and conclude treaties, subject to Senate approval, and requires peaceful settlement and non-use-of-force principles.
evidence.title: Constitución Política de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos
evidence.excerpt: Article 89, fraction X, gives the president authority to direct foreign policy and conclude treaties, subject to Senate approval, and requires peaceful settlement and non-use-of-force principles.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official constitutional text; directly states the executive's foreign-policy power and constraints.
evidence.ruler_attribution: AMLO had treaty-diplomacy authority in 2022, but the legal text is institutional rather than personal nuclear-risk evidence.
contrary_evidence: The Senate remains a real constraint.
These powers concern diplomacy, not weapons custody or nuclear command.

evidence.claim: The official transcript identifies Andrés Manuel López Obrador as the constitutional president of Mexico and commander in chief when he presented the fourth government report from Palacio Nacional.
evidence.title: Versión estenográfica. 4° Informe de Gobierno
evidence.excerpt: The official transcript identifies Andrés Manuel López Obrador as the constitutional president of Mexico and commander in chief when he presented the fourth government report from Palacio Nacional.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official transcript dated the day of the event.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct AMLO attribution, but the content is a self-report rather than independent verification.
contrary_evidence: The report is inherently self-justifying.
It does not show any nuclear-risk decision or safety reform by itself.

evidence.claim: Mexico said the key principles were the prohibition of the threat or use of force, non-intervention, and peaceful settlement of disputes; it said there was no military solution and that diplomatic paths had not been exhausted.
evidence.title: Situation along Russian Federation-Ukraine Border Can Only Be Resolved through Diplomacy, Political Affairs Chief Tells Security Council
evidence.excerpt: Mexico said the key principles were the prohibition of the threat or use of force, non-intervention, and peaceful settlement of disputes; it said there was no military solution and that diplomatic paths had not been exhausted.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN Security Council record of Mexico's official statement.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 fit, just before the invasion escalated into full-scale war.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional Mexican foreign-policy position under AMLO; attributed to Mexico's UN delegation rather than a personal directive from AMLO.
contrary_evidence: Mexico initially framed the issue cautiously and did not endorse immediate coercive measures beyond diplomacy.
This is crisis diplomacy, not proof of unique presidential initiative.

evidence.claim: Mexico condemned the invasion of Ukraine, called for stronger multilateral organizations, and said the situation required states to reaffirm peace and respect for human rights.
evidence.title: Mexico takes part in the UN Human Rights Council High-Level Segment
evidence.excerpt: Mexico condemned the invasion of Ukraine, called for stronger multilateral organizations, and said the situation required states to reaffirm peace and respect for human rights.
evidence.source_locator: Press release bullet points and opening paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary foreign-ministry release dated during the opening phase of the war.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government of Mexico under AMLO; not a direct personal statement by AMLO.
contrary_evidence: This is a broad normative statement, not an operational peace action.
It does not resolve the question of whether later Mexican diplomacy was effective.

evidence.claim: Mexico said it voted in favor of the urgent debate on Ukraine, condemned the invasion and human-rights violations, and said it would keep urging parties to keep diplomatic channels open for a peaceful resolution.
evidence.title: Mexico participates in UN Human Rights Council urgent debate on Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Mexico said it voted in favor of the urgent debate on Ukraine, condemned the invasion and human-rights violations, and said it would keep urging parties to keep diplomatic channels open for a peaceful resolution.
evidence.source_locator: Press release summary and opening paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary release with explicit vote and stated rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mexican state action under AMLO; the statement is made by an undersecretary, so attribution is institutional rather than personal.
contrary_evidence: A vote for debate is not the same as a negotiated settlement.
It does not show AMLO personally driving the action.

evidence.claim: Mexico strongly condemned the invasion, evacuated people from Ukraine by air force aircraft, and said it would not apply unilateral sanctions against another country.
evidence.title: Mexican Air Force plane arrives in Mexico with 81 passengers evacuated from Ukraine: Ebrard
evidence.excerpt: Mexico strongly condemned the invasion, evacuated people from Ukraine by air force aircraft, and said it would not apply unilateral sanctions against another country.
evidence.source_locator: Opening bullet points and first paragraph
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government release tied to a dated evacuation operation and policy statement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government action under AMLO; the evacuation was instructed by the president, but the sanctions line is a government policy position rather than a uniquely personal act.
contrary_evidence: Refusing unilateral sanctions is restraint, but it can also be read as hedging rather than active peace-making.
This does not prove deeper conflict-resolution leverage.

evidence.claim: Mexico said it and France had negotiated a humanitarian draft in good faith; Mexico explained it abstained on the Russian alternative because it omitted Article 2.4 of the UN Charter and an unequivocal cessation of hostilities, and because the balance sought in the original draft was excluded.
evidence.title: Security Council Fails to Adopt Text Demanding Civilian Protection, Unhindered Humanitarian Access in Ukraine, as 13 Members Abstain
evidence.excerpt: Mexico said it and France had negotiated a humanitarian draft in good faith; Mexico explained it abstained on the Russian alternative because it omitted Article 2.4 of the UN Charter and an unequivocal cessation of hostilities, and because the balance sought in the original draft was excluded.
evidence.source_locator: Mexico statement and France/Mexico negotiation references
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN meeting record with explicit Mexico explanation of its position.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mexico's UN delegation under AMLO; this is institutional diplomacy, not a personal military-order decision.
contrary_evidence: Mexico abstained on the Russian alternative rather than backing a hard break with Russia.
The draft remained humanitarian, not a full peace settlement.

evidence.claim: Mexico is listed among the sponsors of the humanitarian draft resolution on Ukraine, which called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, protection of civilians, and respect for international humanitarian law.
evidence.title: Humanitarian consequences of the aggression against Ukraine : draft resolution / Albania ... Mexico ...
evidence.excerpt: Mexico is listed among the sponsors of the humanitarian draft resolution on Ukraine, which called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, protection of civilians, and respect for international humanitarian law.
evidence.source_locator: Authors list and resolution title in the record
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN depositary record directly identifies the co-sponsors and the draft text's subject.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional Mexican sponsorship under AMLO; the text shows state diplomacy rather than AMLO personally drafting it.
contrary_evidence: Sponsorship does not prove the resolution changed the war.
This is a procedural record, so the substantive detail is limited to the title and sponsor list.

evidence.claim: AMLO said the war in Ukraine should have been avoided, said he did not agree with sanctions, and argued the goal should be to stop the war because it harms most peoples.
evidence.title: Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador del 8 de septiembre de 2022
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said the war in Ukraine should have been avoided, said he did not agree with sanctions, and argued the goal should be to stop the war because it harms most peoples.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential transcript with direct quoted statements from AMLO.
contrary_evidence: His criticism of sanctions makes the position more pacific than aligned with coercive anti-aggression policy.
The statement is rhetorical unless tied to subsequent diplomacy.

evidence.claim: AMLO proposed a mediation committee with Narendra Modi, Pope Francis, and the UN Secretary-General to start talks with the presidents of Ukraine and Russia and sought a five-year truce without military exercises, nuclear practices, missiles, interventions, or internal conflict involvement.
evidence.title: Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador del 12 de septiembre de 2022
evidence.excerpt: AMLO proposed a mediation committee with Narendra Modi, Pope Francis, and the UN Secretary-General to start talks with the presidents of Ukraine and Russia and sought a five-year truce without military exercises, nuclear practices, missiles, interventions, or internal conflict involvement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential transcript with a precise, dated peace initiative.
contrary_evidence: Ukraine later opposed the plan as too favorable to Russia, according to independent reporting.
A proposal is not the same as an implemented ceasefire.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Mexican Foreign Minister Marcelo Ebrard met Sergei Lavrov to discuss Mexico's peace plan for Ukraine, which Mexico had presented at the UN General Assembly; Ukraine opposed the plan as advantageous to Russia.
evidence.title: Mexico foreign minister meets Russia's Lavrov to discuss Ukraine peace plan
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Mexican Foreign Minister Marcelo Ebrard met Sergei Lavrov to discuss Mexico's peace plan for Ukraine, which Mexico had presented at the UN General Assembly; Ukraine opposed the plan as advantageous to Russia.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting via Euronews is strong independent confirmation of the diplomatic initiative and the main objection to it.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Mexico's foreign minister and government under AMLO; this is state diplomacy, not a private initiative.
contrary_evidence: Ukraine's objection is material and suggests the plan was contested.
The article does not show the plan had any concrete effect.

evidence.claim: Mexico said it supported Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders and voted in favor of the resolution condemning the referenda and annexation efforts.
evidence.title: Security Council Fails to Adopt Resolution Condemning Moscow's Referenda in Ukraine’s Occupied Territories, as Permanent Member Employs Veto
evidence.excerpt: Mexico said it supported Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders and voted in favor of the resolution condemning the referenda and annexation efforts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN record explicitly notes Mexico's vote and stated rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mexico's Security Council vote under AMLO; institutional foreign policy rather than personal operational control.
contrary_evidence: This is a condemnation vote, not a ceasefire success.
It shows alignment with lawful order more than direct conflict management.

evidence.claim: Mexico said it would abstain from the draft suspending Russia from the Human Rights Council because it wanted all channels maintained for dialogue even in wartime.
evidence.title: General Assembly Adopts Text to Suspend Russian Federation from Human Rights Council, Continuing Emergency Special Session on Humanitarian Crisis in Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Mexico said it would abstain from the draft suspending Russia from the Human Rights Council because it wanted all channels maintained for dialogue even in wartime.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN record quoting Mexico's explanation for abstention.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mexican delegation under AMLO; this is a policy choice at the UN, not a personal command decision.
contrary_evidence: Abstention can be read as preserving dialogue or as reluctance to isolate an aggressor.
It is not a settlement mechanism by itself.

evidence.claim: The AP-reported piece said the Mexico-France humanitarian resolution called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, protection of civilians, and respect for international humanitarian law, and that it passed in the General Assembly.
evidence.title: Mexico, France and the UN humanitarian resolution on Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: The AP-reported piece said the Mexico-France humanitarian resolution called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, protection of civilians, and respect for international humanitarian law, and that it passed in the General Assembly.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: AP-reported local-language coverage corroborates the UN and Mexican-government records with an independent news frame.
contrary_evidence: This is still a humanitarian framework, not a negotiated peace settlement.
The article is derivative of AP reporting rather than an original investigation.

unresolved_gaps: Federal command attribution is still thin for several state-level protest, journalist, and policing incidents.
Independent evidence that AMLO strengthened courts, the INE, INAI, or other checks is still weak compared with the evidence of media hostility and electoral-pressure attempts.
Direct personal-nexus evidence on self-enrichment, hidden ownership, or preferential benefit remains thin, and several items are still allegations or self-reports.
Independent audit-level evidence on on-time, on-budget delivery and the causal split between AMLO policy and external tailwinds is still incomplete.
